contents: # The map platform (uhifadhi/map-module) — self-hosted Leaflet, the basemap
# seam, the boundary drawing and the map chrome every map in the product wears.
# WHICH IMAGERY. Nothing is set here, so every environment gets the bundle's
# default: `esri`, the keyless World Imagery. It draws everywhere, costs
# nothing and needs no account, which is what a fresh installation wants.
# To use Google satellite instead, set the provider in an environment you
# actually hold a key for — typically prod only — and leave the rest on Esri:
#   when@prod:
#       map:
#           satellite:
#               provider: google
#               google:
#                   api_key: '%env(default::UHIFADHI_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY)%'
# The key is public by nature — it travels inside every tile URL — so restrict
# it by HTTP referrer at Google rather than treating it as a secret. An unset
# key is a valid state: the bundle falls back to Esri and asks nobody. Note
# that some accounts and regions are refused satellite outright (a 403 on
# createSession); if that is yours, stay on Esri rather than re-earning the
# refusal on every map.
map:
module_category: operations
# THE THREE IMPORTMAP LINES, WRITTEN FOR YOU — BUT NOT BY THIS RECIPE.
# The bundle registers its own assets/ directory under the AssetMapper
# namespace @uhifadhi/map-module, and importmap entries are read from the
# host's single importmap.php. A recipe cannot write them: recipes copy files
# and patch YAML, and importmap.php is PHP.
# Flex can, and does. uhifadhi/map-module declares the entries itself, in its
# assets/package.json under symfony.importmap, and Flex runs importmap:require
# once per entry on install — the same mechanism symfony/stimulus-bundle uses
# for its loader. Nothing is added by hand any more. What lands in
# importmap.php is:
#   'uhifadhi/basemaps'   => ['path' => './vendor/uhifadhi/map-module/assets/basemaps.js'],
#   'uhifadhi/boundary'   => ['path' => './vendor/uhifadhi/map-module/assets/boundary.js'],
#   'uhifadhi/map-chrome' => ['path' => './vendor/uhifadhi/map-module/assets/chrome.js'],
# (The vendor-relative path is what importmap:require stores; the logical path
# @uhifadhi/map-module/basemaps.js names the same file and is equally valid if
# you ever write one by hand.)
# It needs the host to HAVE an importmap.php — a host running AssetMapper. A
# host that installed the bundle for the Leaflet build alone has nothing to
# write into and gets nothing written, which is correct.
# The keys are bare specifiers on purpose: every importer — the host's own map
# controllers and each module's map — imports the NAME, never the path, so the
# files can move underneath them without touching a single import site.
